title: Gov. Braun to assess storm damage and coordinate resources in Hammond on Aug. 12
text:
Gov. Braun to assess storm damage and coordinate resources in Hammond on Aug. 12
Indiana Governor Mike Braun, along with Adjutant General of the Indiana National Guard Larry Muennich, Superintendent of State Police Anthony Scott, and Department of Homeland Security Executive Director Jonathan Whitham, will join first responders and local officials to assess severe storm damage and coordinate necessary resources in Hammond on Aug. 12.
According to an advisory from the Office of Governor Mike Braun, the governor has directed the Indiana Department of Homeland Security to lead the state's response efforts. This includes collaboration with the Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Indiana State Police, Indiana National Guard, Indiana Department of Transportation, and the Indiana Department of Correction.
The assessment will take place at Hammond Central Fire Station located at 6110 Calumet Ave., Hammond. The event is scheduled for Wednesday at 12:30 PM Central Time. Media representatives are required to RSVP with Press Secretary Griffin Reid.
Braun contributed to public service through roles on school boards and in state representation; he achieved growth of his company into a national entity employing thousands; championed over 40 bills that became law during his Senate term; has been married for 49 years and raised four children; won election to the U.S. Senate in 2018 before becoming governor; and graduated summa cum laude with a degree in economics from Wabash College before earning an MBA from Harvard Business School, according to the official website.
Griffin Reid serves as press secretary for Governor Braun's office.
